svg.aria-label: Diagram of three accounts. The management account holds the organisation and as little else as possible. The security tooling account is the delegated administrator for the detective services, configuring detection across member accounts and running response automation. The log archive account receives what detection produces and the security tooling account cannot delete from it. The separation exists so that management and usage of the log privileges sit in different accounts. At the bottom, the growth problem: an account that begins as read-only detection accumulates response roles into every member account, so the account whose job is watching ends up with the broadest write reach in the organisation.
svg.title: Why detection is configured in one account and its output stored in another, and how the tooling account quietly becomes the most powerful one
svg.text: Configuring detection and storing its output are different jobs
Put them in one account and its administrator can both switch the trail off and delete what it already wrote.
Management account
The organisation, and as close to
nothing else as you can manage.
No SCP reaches it. Deploy elsewhere.
Security tooling account
Delegated administrator for the
detective services. Configures
detection, and acts on it.
It manages the trail.
Log archive account
Holds the trail's output, the Config
snapshots, the exported findings.
Object Lock. Nobody writes.
It owns the output.
AWS states the reason in one line. The tooling account is the delegated administrator for CloudTrail; the bucket lives in
the log archive account, and this is to separate the management and usage of CloudTrail log privileges.
What gets delegated there
GuardDuty · Security Hub · Security Hub CSPM · IAM Access Analyzer · Amazon Detective · Amazon Macie · Amazon Inspector ·
AWS Config · AWS CloudTrail · Firewall Manager · Audit Manager · Systems Manager · Security Incident Response · centralized
management of root access
The drift nobody schedules a review for
This account starts as read-only detection, which is easy to approve. Then response automation arrives, and response means a role
in every member account that this one can assume — to isolate an instance, revoke a key, quarantine a bucket. Each grant is
justified on its own. Added up, the account whose job is watching holds the broadest write reach in the organisation.
Unlike the management account, this one is a member account — so SCPs do bind it, which is the only reason the drift is containable.
